Hi Alex — quick technical notes before Rishi provides the cost breakdown:

- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming keeps client perceived latency low because tokens are delivered as generated; operationally it requires more aggressive CPU/GPU pinning and increases utilization inefficiencies (so higher $/1M). Non-streaming with batching benefits from higher throughput but adds batching latency (configurable).
- Batching settings: continuous batching with small max-delay (20–50ms) often hits a good balance: reduces cost by ~15–30% vs single-request dispatching while keeping added latency within your P95 target for many workloads. Larger batch windows (100–200ms) save more but will push P95 above 400ms for short completions.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching can dramatically reduce token cost for repeated prompts (30–60% savings in some flows).

Looping Rishi for concrete unit economics and SLA-tier implications.

—Priyom

Alex — thanks for the details. Below are three illustrative scenarios (ballpark numbers to help you evaluate economics). All numbers assume our verified open model family (static model profile) and include typical batching/caching improvements we can enable for the given SLOs. Final pricing depends on model choice and whether you want Dedicated pools or Hosted with SLO-backed routing.

1) Low-latency premium (P95 <= 250–350ms, streaming enabled)
- Unit price: $18–$24 per 1M tokens
- Rationale: streaming + strict pinning / reserved capacity increases unit cost.
- Example monthly cost: 120M tokens -> $2,160–$2,880; 900M tokens -> $16,200–$21,600
- Recommended for: customer-facing chat where token-level latency is critical.

2) Balanced (P95 <= 350–450ms, small continuous batching 20–50ms, partial streaming for long outputs)
- Unit price: $9–$12 per 1M tokens
- Rationale: modest batching and prefix caching reduce cost while keeping P95 within your stated 400ms target for most short completions.
- Example monthly cost: 120M tokens -> $1,080–$1,440; 900M tokens -> $8,100–$10,800
- Recommended for: mixed customer-facing + internal flows where cost matters and a modest latency trade is acceptable.

3) Cost-optimized (P95 up to ~800ms, larger batching windows, aggressive caching, non-streaming)
- Unit price: $4–$7 per 1M tokens
- Rationale: large batches and aggressive caching reduce unit cost. Not suitable for low-latency interactive features.
- Example monthly cost: 120M tokens -> $480–$840; 900M tokens -> $3,600–$6,300
- Recommended for: batched analytics, nightly jobs, back-office workflows.

Additional notes on Dedicated vs Hosted with SLOs:
- Hosted (SLO-backed routing): pay per-token with an SLO uplift for guaranteed P95; good for quick onboarding.
- Dedicated (reserved pools): monthly commit + lower unit price at high volume; required if you need strict isolation and predictable latency at scale.

Quick calc against your $10k–$25k/month budget for 120M tokens:
- Low-latency premium: $2.2k–$2.9k (within budget) — note this scales linearly, so 900M/month could exceed budget unless you move to reserved pricing.
- Balanced: $1.1k–$1.4k (well within budget).
- Cost-optimized: $480–$840 (well under budget).

If your stated target was ~ $8–$10 per 1M tokens, the Balanced tier aligns nicely. For P95 <=400ms with streaming for long responses we’d expect costs closer to the higher end of that band.

I attached a short SLA tier comparison and a sample calculator. Happy to run a custom spreadsheet with your exact prompt lengths and traffic shape. If you’d like I can model both Hosted SLO pricing and an estimated Dedicated commit level to compare the point where reserved capacity becomes cheaper.
